The strongest direct evidence is instead about food aid diversion, housing demolitions/forced evictions, and emergency detentions.","evidence":[{"title":"World Bank backs Ethiopia’s reforms to promote sustainable and inclusive growth","publisher":"World Bank","date":"2024-07-30","url":"https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/07/30/world-bank-backs-ethiopia-s-reforms-to-promote-sustainable-and-inclusive-afe-growth","summary":"The package explicitly aimed to expand social safety nets, improve public-spending effectiveness, and protect poor and vulnerable households, with rural access improvements across all 13 regions and 50% of intended beneficiaries identified as women. This is broad-based allocation logic, not obvious loyalty targeting.","question_ids":["6B.7","6B.2","6B.3","6B.4","6B.5"]},{"title":"Ethiopia signs 172 billion USD financing agreements with the World Bank","publisher":"Ethiopia Ministry of Finance","date":"2024-04-05","url":"https://www.mofed.gov.et/blog/ethiopia-signs-172-billion-usd-financing-agreements-with-the-world-bank/","summary":"The ministry said the funds would go to rural connectivity, food security, adaptive safety nets, power-sector reform, and water/sanitation. That is evidence of a public-good allocation strategy rather than naked patronage.","question_ids":["6B.7","6B.2","6B.4","6B.5"]},{"title":"Ethiopia Country Profile 2024","publisher":"World Health Organization","date":"2024","url":"https://www.who.int/about/accountability/results/who-results-report-2024-2025/country-profile/2024/ethiopia","summary":"WHO says it supported Ethiopia to strengthen primary health care, improve service delivery, and track health expenditures and barriers for decision-making. That supports a more rule-based, less patronage-like approach to social services.","question_ids":["6B.7","6B.4","6B.5"]},{"title":"ILO trains social health protection actors in Ethiopia","publisher":"United Nations in Ethiopia / ILO","date":"2024-07-19","url":"https://ethiopia.un.org/en/277133-ilo-trains-social-health-protection-actors-ethiopia","summary":"Policymakers and administrators running social health protection were trained to strengthen financing and protection systems. This is technical capacity-building, not evidence of benefits being reserved for loyalists.","question_ids":["6B.7","6B.4","6B.5"]},{"title":"World Report 2024: Ethiopia","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"2024","url":"https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/ethiopia","summary":"HRW says WFP and USAID halted food aid after a “widespread and coordinated scheme” by federal and regional actors to divert aid, with reports that military units benefited from the diversion. That is strong evidence that a core welfare channel was compromised and could function as a political/resource tool.","question_ids":["6B.7","6B.2","6B.6","6B.4"]},{"title":"World Report 2024: Ethiopia","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"2024","url":"https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/ethiopia","summary":"The same report says Oromia authorities demolished homes and businesses in Shegar city, rendering residents homeless, and that people protesting the demolitions were beaten and shot. That is strong evidence that housing and land-related state action was coercive, not welfare-protective.","question_ids":["6B.7","6B.2","6B.6","6B.3"]},{"title":"Ethiopia: Authorities must stop using state of emergency law to silence peaceful dissent","publisher":"Amnesty International","date":"2024-02-19","url":"https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/02/ethiopia-authorities-must-stop-using-state-of-emergency-law-to-silence-peaceful-dissent/","summary":"Amnesty says the state of emergency gave authorities sweeping power to arrest without warrant, impose curfews, restrict movement, and ban assemblies, and that it was used to detain critics and journalists. That is direct evidence of state power being used punitively against dissent rather than neutrally administering public benefits.","question_ids":["6B.7","6B.5","6B.6","6B.3"]},{"title":"Ethiopia: End the month-long arbitrary detention of thousands in Amhara Region","publisher":"Amnesty International","date":"2024-11-06","url":"https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/11/ethiopia-end-the-month-long-arbitrary-detention-of-thousands-in-amhara-region/","summary":"Amnesty says a joint federal-regional task force filled makeshift detention camps with thousands of civilians and described mass detention as a routine political tool under emergency laws. That is strong evidence of punitive state control, which is relevant to whether jobs, permits, and benefits were insulated from loyalty enforcement.","question_ids":["6B.7","6B.5","6B.6","6B.3"]},{"title":"World Report 2024: Ethiopia","publisher":"Freedom House","date":"2024","url":"https://freedomhouse.org/country/ethiopia/freedom-world/2024","summary":"Freedom House says corruption and unequal resource distribution are significant problems, and that food-aid distribution has been impacted by official corruption. This is weaker than the HRW/Amnesty items, but it supports a broader pattern of non-neutral state allocation.","question_ids":["6B.7","6B.4","6B.5"]}]}
